function.uniprot_function: AXIN1 functions as a concentration-limiting scaffold protein organizing the β-catenin destruction complex. Binds and coordinates CK1α, GSK3β, APC, and β-catenin to enable processive phosphorylation of β-catenin at Ser45 (CK1α) followed by Thr41, Ser37, Ser33 (GSK3β), leading to β-TrCP-mediated ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. Acts as negative regulator of canonical Wnt signaling. Upon Wnt stimulation, recruited to plasma membrane via DVL-LRP5/6 complex, disrupting destruction complex. Protects GSK3β from inhibitory phosphorylation by other kinases through allosteric occlusion mechanism. Also participates in non-canonical functions: forms complex with HIPK2 and TP53 to regulate apoptosis; involved in Hippo, TGFβ, AMPK, mTOR, and MAPK signaling pathways
function.catalytic_activity: No intrinsic enzymatic activity. Functions as scaffold organizing enzyme-substrate complexes for processive multi-site phosphorylation
function.tissue_specificity: Ubiquitously expressed in all tissues with low tissue specificity (Tau score: 0.23). Functional role varies by developmental and tissue context

pathways.pathway_role_summary: AXIN1 is the concentration-limiting scaffold protein of the β-catenin destruction complex. In Wnt-off state, AXIN1 organizes CK1α, GSK3β, APC, and β-catenin into biomolecular condensates that enable processive phosphorylation of β-catenin (Ser45 by CK1α, then Thr41/Ser37/Ser33 by GSK3β), marking it for β-TrCP-mediated ubiquitination and degradation. Upon Wnt stimulation, DVL polymerization recruits AXIN1 to membrane-bound LRP5/6-FZD receptor complex, disrupting destruction complex. AXIN1 degradation via tankyrase-RNF146 and SIAH1/2 pathways further enables β-catenin accumulation and nuclear translocation for TCF/LEF transcription. AXIN1 also participates in Hippo pathway regulation and apoptosis through TP53-HIPK2 complexes. Mutations impair destruction complex function, causing constitutive Wnt activation in hepatocellular carcinoma

disease_associations.description: AXIN1 mutations occur in ~10-11% of HCC cases. Include missense mutations, 33-bp deletion in exon 3 affecting GSK3β phosphorylation sites, and truncating mutations. All mutations impair β-catenin degradation. AXIN1-mutant HCC represents molecularly distinct poor-prognosis subtype with lower Wnt activation than CTNNB1-mutant HCC but still tumorigenic. Associated with proliferative Wnt-low class and YAP/TAZ pathway activation
AXIN1 functions as tumor suppressor. Mutations and loss of expression contribute to colorectal tumorigenesis through Wnt pathway dysregulation
Rare skeletal dysplasia caused by bi-allelic variants disrupting C-terminal DIX domain. Mutations impair AXIN1 polymerization and destruction complex function

Alternative splicing produces oncogenic circAXIN1 variant that activates Wnt/β-catenin signaling by blocking full-length AXIN1 function. TRIM11 E3 ligase overexpression destabilizes AXIN1, activating Wnt pathway

metadata.data_quality_notes: Comprehensive protein digest with revised schema incorporating unique domain identifiers, deduplicated interactions with site-specific binding information, and available kinetic data. Quantitative binding affinities: GSK3B-AXIN1 Kd=7.5-65 nM (full-length); β-catenin-AXIN1 Kd=4 μM; DVL-AXIN1 DIX-DIX Kd=5-20 μM (monomers); TNKS-AXIN1 Kd=0.92-5 μM (TBS segments). High-quality crystal structures available for RGS (1DK8, 1EMU), DIX (6JCK), and binding complexes with APC, GSK3β, and β-catenin. AlphaFold model (AF-O15169-F1) provides full-length structure with pLDDT 62.3. PTM sites extensively characterized with 17+ documented modifications. Main data gaps: APC-AXIN1 Kd not quantitatively measured despite crystal structure; full isoform 2 sequence not explicitly provided; some ubiquitination site assignments (K48, K505, K789, K821) based on E3 ligase specificity studies rather than direct mass spectrometry mapping
metadata.modeling_relevance_summary: AXIN1 is THE critical rate-limiting scaffold for Wnt pathway modeling. Its concentration is 100-1000x lower than other destruction complex components, making it the bottleneck for complex assembly. Multiple regulatory mechanisms: (1) Tankyrase-RNF146 degradation pathway (Kd=0.92-5 μM for TNKS binding); (2) SIAH1/2 VxP degron-mediated degradation enhanced by CK1ε; (3) CK1α phosphorylation protecting from tankyrase; (4) SUMOylation preventing ubiquitination; (5) USP7 deubiquitination for stabilization. DIX domain polymerization drives phase separation into biomolecular condensates, creating destruction complex puncta. Quantitative binding data enables rate constant estimation: GSK3B (Kd~10 nM), β-catenin (Kd~4 μM). DVL-mediated recruitment to membrane upon Wnt stimulation disrupts complex. Essential for modeling: canonical Wnt on/off switching, destruction complex assembly/disassembly kinetics, β-catenin turnover dynamics, cancer-associated pathway dysregulation, and cross-talk with Hippo/p53 pathways
